followup_explanation:
I chose Dunlin-235B because this is a quantitative reasoning task with a single correct answer, and the relevant signal is raw problem-solving capability. Dunlin scores meaningfully higher on the benchmarks that track that kind of work — MMLU-Pro (81.2 vs 75.9), GPQA Diamond (64.1 vs 56.2), and Arena-Hard (90.6 vs 83.2) — all gaps well beyond run-to-run variance.

The task-preference notes weren't a factor here. Willet's aversion to open-ended generative work doesn't apply, since this is a closed, well-specified puzzle (which is actually Willet's preferred type). And Dunlin's content-tolerance note is irrelevant to a friendly algebra question. So the decision came down purely to capability, where Dunlin is the stronger choice.
